data.name: Mayukhi
data.gender_notes: Mayukhi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Mayukhi is the name of the goddess of beauty and prosperity in Hindu mythology. Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘mai’, meaning ‘mother’, and ‘yuk’ meaning ‘beauty’, this name symbolizes the grace and charm of a mother. It is also believed that invoking the blessings of Mayukhi bestows upon one the gifts of beauty, longevity, and prosperity.
data.spiritual_meaning: Blessings of the Goddess of Beauty and Prosperity
data.etymology: Mayukhi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Beauty.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mayukhi total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

Mayukhi is often depicted as a young, radiant, and lovely goddess, adorned with ornaments and flowers. In several Hindu rituals and customs, the name Mayukhi is invoked to seek blessings of beauty, fertility, and prosperity.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Mayukhi lies in its connection to the divine power of beauty and nurturing. In Hindu mythology, Mayukhi is believed to be the embodiment of motherly love and grace. Invoking her blessings is said to bring about inner and outer beauty, along with nourishment and prosperity. Mayukhi is also a symbol of the divine feminine, representing the power of creation and preservation in the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mayukhi: Goddess of beauty and radiance, symbolizing inner and outer grace. Her name, derived from the Sanskrit word 'mai' (giving) and 'yuk' (connection), signifies one who connects and nurtures beauty within and around.

historical_references.reference: Mayukhi is a Hindu name derived from the Sanskrit word 'mayush' which means 'growth' or 'long life'. It is a popular name in India and is given to girls as a wish for their long and prosperous life.

Another reference for the name Mayukhi is found in the Hindu epic Mahabharata. Mayukhi is the name of a celestial nymph or apsara who is known for her beauty and charm. She is described as the daughter of the Himalayas and is often depicted as holding a lotus flower and adorned with precious jewels.
